newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 4.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page on April 4:
WASHINGTON - George Washington University announced that it has entered into a $125 million agreement to sell its 153-year-old hospital to one of the nation's largest health care chains.

WASHINGTON - Maryland's Democratic-controlled General Assembly embraced a theme usually promoted by Republicans, giving final approval to a plan to cut the state's standard income tax rate below 5 percent for the first time since 1967.
WASHINGTON - As a group, children in day care learn to think and talk just as well as those cared for by their mothers, a long-term national study has found.

WASHINGTON - Two senior White House aides were acting out of compassion when they tried to line up lucrative employment for Webster Hubbell after his resignation from the Justice Department, President Clinton said.

JERUSALEM - Israel gave up its bid for extradition of a senior Hamas leader from the United States, citing the same concerns over security and the prevention of terrorist attacks that inspired the initial request nearly two years ago.

MEXICO CITY - Swiss prosecutors have concluded after months of investigation that Raul Salinas de Gotari, the brother of Mexico's former president, received huge sums of money in exchange for helping Mexican drug traffickers, according to senior Mexican law enforcement officials.
